Hi Lena —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, operational reply; I'll attach our internal playbook and a short checklist. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through this.

High-level answers:

1) Region pinning and replication
- When a tenant is provisioned on a Dedicated pool, the placement key (region tag + cluster id) is set in the control plane and enforced by our scheduler. For US-central Dedicated deployments we default to single-region anchoring unless customer requests multi-region DR.
- Replication: By default we do not replicate persistent tenant data to other geographic regions. Snapshots for backup are stored in the same region by default; cross-region replication must be explicitly enabled in the contract and requires storage-level encryption keys and approvals.

2) Tenant wipe timeline and scope
- Standard wipe workflow: (a) quiesce traffic and revoke tokens, (b) take final-forensic snapshot with an immutable flag, (c) delete live KV & object storage, (d) purge snapshots and release disk leases, (e) run checksum audit and provide deletion attestations.
- Estimated timelines: live data purge typically completes within 4–12 hours depending on dataset size and throughput; snapshot purges can take 12–72 hours depending on retention tiers and glacier-like archives.

3) Eviction & rollback
- Live-eviction: we first isolate the tenant network and suspend new allocations. We then create an immutable forensic snapshot (read-only) before any modification. Rollback options are limited once deletion is authorized — we never automatically rehydrate data to another region without explicit signed consent.
- Forensic access: we can create a sealed evidence package for legal teams; any access is logged with per-request signatures and requires a legal hold ticket.
- Avoiding leakage: snapshots are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) if requested, and we zero crypto-material on any deleted volumes prior to reuse.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-local-delete-playbook.pdf (pdf) — contains the step-by-step checklist + audit log references.

Lena — adding ops detail and the checklist (inline) for clarity. Sean's note is accurate; operational notes below.

Operational checklist (tenant wipe, single-region default):
- [ ] Create incident ticket in Ops queue (TAG: HB-tenant-wipe)
- [ ] Quiesce workload and mark ingress endpoints read-only
- [ ] Revoke service tokens, rotate API keys
- [ ] Snapshot with immutable flag -> store in region's archive (retention window 7 days unless otherwise requested)
- [ ] Delete object storage containers (list of prefixes attached in ticket) -> mark for immediate purge
- [ ] Delete DB KV shards and zero disks on node pool
- [ ] Trigger snapshot purge process -> monitor for external archive tiers (may take longer)
- [ ] Run deletion audit (sha256 manifests) and attach manifest to ticket
- [ ] Produce attestation PDF and provide signed timestamped log bundle

Timeline notes: large datasets (>5TB) can be staged for parallel purge; we provide mid-point progress updates at 2-hour cadence. If KMS-backed keys exist, we prefer crypto-shredding (key destruction) as the final attestation layer.

Attachment: tenant-wipe-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet) — operational columns for runbook steps and owners.

Happy to join a call to walk this through with your SREs.
